verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_jump_analyzer_test_video: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter and terse names in core logic (`g`, `M`, `h`, `w`, `dil`, `cnt`). No docstrings on `analyze_video` or `main`. Some helpful inline comments, e.g. "Bottom strip of the track ... has no runner".

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `analyze_video` is one function of about 100 lines that reads the video, aligns frames, segments the athlete and detects takeoff/landing. This ignores the requested split into a measurement function and a detection function. Stray `output.toml` artifact committed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Has a `cap.isOpened()` check and raises `RuntimeError` instead of swallowing errors. Many unnamed magic constants: `diff > 35.0`, `0.70`, `0.73`, `cnt > 1000`, `>= 3000`, `t_peak - 12`, `ground_pre - 8`, `(25, 25)` kernel.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: Checks `isOpened`; raises `RuntimeError` on too few frames or no athlete (uncaught, but non-zero exit with a message). All thresholds are absolute pixel constants tuned to the example video, and the hidden test failed.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads the positional input path and always writes `/app/output.toml` with exactly the two `int` fields. Frame numbers are 0-based (from `enumerate`) and this is never stated; the reference counts from 1. With no argument it silently falls back to `example_video.mp4`.
